title: Exemplar Pruning — Gambit Lab Notes
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal lab for systematically pruning few-shot exemplars to reduce token cost while preserving response quality on our customer support and summarization tasks.
- Try lightweight heuristics (semantic redundancy, label diversity, influence proxies) before heavier retraining/selection pipelines.

Notes on motivation:
- Many client prompts use 6–8 exemplars by default; unit token cost is high and latency increases because of context size.
- Some exemplars are noisy/contradictory and actually degrade answers (observed in INF-433 evals).
- Goal: get to a 2–3 exemplar “core” for each intent cluster with minimal quality drop.

Experiment ideas (quick list):
1) Redundancy filter (fast)
   - Embed all exemplars with embed-v2, cluster at cosine > 0.92, keep 1 representative per cluster.
   - Pros: cheap, stable. Cons: may drop edge-case coverage.

2) Label diversity score
   - For tasks with categorical labels (intent, tone), score sets by label coverage + inverse frequency weighting.
   - Prefer sets that maximize rare-label representation.

3) Influence proxy via leave-one-out prompting (slow):
   - For each exemplar e_i, measure delta in metric (accuracy/ROUGE/QA F1) when removing e_i from set of N.
   - Rank exemplars by positive delta and prune negatives.

4) Mix-and-match annealing (stochastic):
   - Randomly sample candidate subsets (k=2..4), evaluate on 50 held examples, keep Pareto sets.

5) Heuristic rules for position sensitivity:
   - Keep exemplars that perform well both when shown first and last (some models overweight first exemplars).

Quick protocol for runs:
- Dataset: 2k validation samples from support-triage and 1k for summarization test.
- Model: rwi-llm-small (quantized prod variant) and rwi-llm-medium (for stability check).
- Metrics: intent accuracy, slot-F1 (where applicable), and human-eval precision for 200 samples (binary: acceptable / not acceptable).
- Budget: aim for total context tokens <= 1.2k in trimmed prompts.

Preliminary observations (hand-run, noisy):
- Redundancy filter reduced exemplars from 6->3 with ~1.8% drop in intent accuracy but 0.4s median latency reduction.
- Leave-one-out showed 2 exemplars with negative or zero marginal value; one exemplar was contradictory (older policy example).
- Annealing found a 3-exemplar set that matched baseline on intent but beat it for a rare sub-intent (billing-dispute).

Failure cases and gotchas:
- Semantic-embedding clustering sometimes groups together exemplars with opposite labels if wording is similar ("refund approved" vs "refund requested"). Need label-aware distance.
- Removing exemplars that contain edge-case phrasing hurts robustness on customer support transcripts with ASR noise.
- Position/order matters more than I expected for rwi-llm-small; medium is more stable.

Actionable next steps (short):
- Implement label-aware redundancy: weighted distance where same label halves distance penalty.
- Run a 10x annealing sweep across 5 intent clusters (validation size 500 each) and save top-5 subsets.
- Create a small human-eval rubric for acceptability w/ 3 annotators on 200 examples.
- Add a quick automated check that flags exemplars with contradictory label tokens (simple regex heuristics).

To dos / notes to self:
- TODO: sync with Priya on INF-8673 about training data refresh and whether older exemplars should be retired.
- TODO: PR to prompt-bank to add metadata field "created_by" + "policy_version" for exemplar provenance.
- Note: check example ordering experiments in /shared_drives/engineering/developer-experience/prompt-ordering-experiments (might overlap).

Mini examples (raw) — baseline set (N=6) -> candidate pruned (N=3):
- Baseline prompt snippet:
  "Example 1: Customer asked for refund because item damaged. Response: apologize, offer refund, escalate if needed"
- Candidate core (3):
  1) "Request refund for damaged item — response: refund approved after photo"
  2) "Cancel subscription refund — offer prorated refund + instructions"
  3) "Charge dispute (card) — escalate to billing ops with case ID"

Notes: candidate core removes ambiguous historical example that suggested "store credit" which conflicts with current policy.

Open questions (for next sync):
- Is a one-size-pruning policy acceptable, or should we tune per-customer profile?
- How to automatically detect exemplars that are "policy stale"? (date heuristics, manual tags, or model-checking against canonical policy snippet)
- Can we build a tiny classifier to predict exemplar marginal value from metadata + embedding (cheap proxy for leave-one-out)?

Relevant links and references (quick):
- INF-433 internal eval notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/INF-433
- Prompt bank PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-bank/pull/142
- Slack thread: #prompt-lab (see thread ts 1678238543)

Random ideas to try later:
- Exemplar condensation via auto-summarization: compress pairs into a condensed exemplar that covers two cases.
- Use retrieval-augmented exemplar selection: retrieve k nearest exemplar candidates to the query then prune on-the-fly.

End of notes.

-- a.m.
